journal_lines: §aSmelled rain before I smelled the trees. §oOak and wet leaf, a whole season stored in the bark.§o Good stand. Clean work.
§aBirch grove, white trunks in rows. Quiet in a way that makes you work quietly too.
§aOak at the center of the grove, wider than I expected. Took the branches. Left the trunk.
§aThe axe went through birch clean. §o§lBirch§l splits easy, smells like green water.§o Good timber.
§aAcorns in the litter underfoot. The squirrels had left some. I left them back.
§aSap came up amber at the cut. Slow and steady. §lOak§l sap always takes its time.
§aFog in the lower branches. §oSmelled like old wood and cold morning.§o Worked until it lifted.
§aBirch bark peels in long curls. Some came off in the work. Brought a few back.
§aGood straight grain in the young oaks. Took three. Left the older ones.
§aThe grove felt like it had been there longer than the surrounding trees. Took only what I needed.
